 --> First Tick: Top global cues to watch in today's trade
 Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) snapped their two-day buying streak on October 29, selling equities worth Rs 943 crore. Meanwhile, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) extended their buying streak to a second consecutive session, purchasing equities worth Rs 1,924 crore. 
 Rakesh Patil 
 October 30, 2026 / 07:36 IST Share --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 Market Today 
 Indian benchmark indices are likely to open on a muted note on October 30, tracking GIFT Nifty, which is up about 55 points at 23,023.50 in early trade.
 Track the latest updates on  GIFT Nifty right here on Moneycontrol 
 Indian equity benchmarks staged a strong rebound on October 29, with the Nifty closing above the 22,900 mark amid broad-based buying across sectors, barring auto stocks.
 Amid mixed global cues, the market opened on a muted note but gained momentum as the session progressed, led by IT and banking stocks. Sentiment was supported after the US Federal Reserve kept its key policy rate unchanged in the 3.75–4% range, in line with market expectations.
 At close, the Sensex was up 905.01 points or 1.24 percent at 74,151.04, and the Nifty was up 237.90 points or 1.05 percent at 22,936.75.
 Related Stories
 Reliance Industries adds 762 points to Sensex, 198 to Nifty in single-day rally 
 Taking Stock: Nifty ends above 23,400, Sensex jumps 1,233 pts; RIL gains most since April 2020 
 Live: RIL sees biggest single-day gain since April 2020; Oct sales cheer auto stocks | Closing Bell 
 The broader markets performed in line with the main indices, with Nifty midcap and smallcap indices rising 1 percent each.
 Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight: GIFT Nifty (Down) 
 GIFT Nifty was trading marginally lower at around 23,023.50 in early trade, indicating a flat to negative start for the domestic equity markets.
 Asian Markets (Down) 
 Asian indices were trading weak in the early trade on Friday, with Taiwan and Nikkei indices down 3 percent and 2 percent, respectively.
 The Kospi Index in South Korea — a key barometer of the AI trade — fell almost 5%, with chip heavyweights Samsung and SK Hynix Inc. declining. That dragged the MSCI Asia Pacific Index down 1.8%.
 US Equities (Slip) 
 US stocks slid on Thursday, with investors reassessing big tech's massive AI spending spree as they digested high-profile ‌earnings and crucial inflation data the day after the Federal Reserve held US interest rates steady.
 All three major US equity indexes lost ground, with the tech-laden Nasdaq losing the most in the wake of Alphabet's disappointing quarterly results released late Wednesday.
 The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 132.54 points, ‌or 0.25%, ⁠to 52,342.56; the S&P 500 lost 23.59 points, or 0.30%, to 7,720.39 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 365.13 points, or 1.37%, to 26,184.72.
 Dollar Index (Down) 
 The dollar index was trading lower against the other major currencies in the early Friday trade.
 US Bond Yield (Down) 
 Yields on 10-year Treasuries shed 4.5 basis points at 4.89 percent, while yields on 2-year Treasuries slipped more than 3 basis points at 4.58 percent.
 Asian Currencies (Up) 
 Asian currencies were trading mostly higher against the US dollar, with most regional currencies strengthening against the greenback. The Malaysian Ringgit emerged as the top gainer, appreciating 0.425 percent, followed by the Indonesian Rupiah, which rose 0.259 percent. The South Korean Won gained 0.218 percent, while the Singapore Dollar and Thai Baht advanced 0.141 percent and 0.134 percent, respectively.
 The Japanese Yen and Philippine Peso also strengthened by 0.312 percent and 0.327 percent, respectively. China's Renminbi edged up 0.084 percent. However, the Taiwan Dollar weakened 0.358 percent.
 Crude (Jumps) 
 Oil rose on signs the US may resume military strikes against Iran, risking fresh turbulence in the region that may hurt energy flows.
 Brent advanced above $115 a barrel after swinging more than $3 in the previous session, while West Texas Intermediate was near $103..
 Gold (Slips) 
 Gold steadied near $4,000 an ounce, and was on track for a second monthly loss, as energy-led inflation raised the prospects for a US rate increase before year-end.
 Bullion was little changed after shedding 1.1% in the previous session.
 The Federal Reserve left the door open for an interest-rate hike before the end of the year to rein in stubborn inflation, and data released Thursday showed a 0.5% rise in the US personal consumption expenditures price index last month. That’s the most since March.
 The Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 in favor of holding its benchmark federal funds rate, while Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said the central bank would likely reduce the number of interest-rate decisions to six from eight per year — a move that analysts said could foster more uncertainty.
 Fund Flow Action 
 Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) snapped their two-day buying streak on October 29, selling equities worth Rs 943 crore. Meanwhile, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) extended their buying streak to a second consecutive session, purchasing equities worth Rs 1,924 crore.
